items.note: The plan states the eight-row schedule, y_S+x_S whatever the scratch values, and forward/inverse/forward giving (x,y)->(-y,x) with scratch restored, as at 728-739 and 761-764. But it only quotes the conclusion 'both net maps are y<-y+x'. It never gives the net change (JV+RG)x, the neighbour rules or the coefficient cancellation (|S∩T| mod 2, or (|S∩T|-1)/2, cancelled by the side wires) at 744-759 that makes the net map the identity.

S1.1.2 states the result as the paper does: frames D_v, edge operator D_vD_u^{-1}, implemented operator D_out S D_in^{-1}. Its method is the paper's invariant argument through sources, edges and pointwise gates (804-817), and S1.1.2.2 covers the endpoint-only conclusion at 818-825.

The plan states comparable nondegenerate labels, the central 3->4 edges as the only decreasing edges (each losing h), L=Ich, the sum Wm-2N+2L and the ratios 100/539 and 101/539, matching 997-1007 and 1105-1110. The telescoping and the use of t_X ⊥ t_Y follow 1048-1071. Missing are the stage labels (eq:motif-labels, 975-988), the residual table (1022-1043) and the orthonormal-basis assertion over F_2 (1073-1102). S1.1.3.1 also gives the inner-product formula of the rational form for both label fields.

Every element of the paper's proof is present. These are projections P_U with -P_{U_a} at the sources, rank of P_V-P_U equal to dim V - dim U, and the N source edges as the only exceptions. The plan also has s_b=W_b m-N+2L_b with deficit N-2L_b>0, the endpoint identity P_{U_a^⊥}-(-P_{U_a})=I_m, and the frame Φ_M (1115-1171).

The statement matches 1214-1228: one kernel aI+bX_v or its inverse per orthonormal residual vector, s_c=W_c m-2N+2L_c with deficit 2N-2L_c, and C^{⊗m} on every role after corrections. The plan derives it from orthogonal weight additivity (1232-1245). It omits the step H diag(1,-1)H=X that turns the character into translation (1254-1257), and the X_a->Y_a correction on the 27 support coordinates via C=iZC^{-1}Z (1290-1310). It also omits negating the X outputs and undoing the exchange (1311-1314).

The plan follows the paper's route: L/N<1/2 gives s_b<W_b m and s_c<W_c m, the relative deficits eta, both above 20*2^{-50}, then m^{1-2^{-50}}>m(1-20*2^{-50})>m(1-eta) from log m<20, so s/W<m^tau with tau=sigma=1-2^{-50}. The exact eta fractions are not reproduced, but the defining inequality is.

Stream operations and controlled shifts appear only as relied-on concepts and as the tool for linear-time triangular updates. The plan never states the list of O(V) operations or the controlled-shift condition (offset prepared in b^{O(1)} time).

Both lemmas are stated correctly. The shear-cost proof is followed closely: triangular factors as controlled shifts in descending order, and each one of Pi as D_j+=H_i, swap, D_j=H_i-D_j (1425-1446). The factorization A=E_1 Pi E_2 is only asserted (S2.1 is an infer step), so the elimination proof at 1375-1392 is missing. The fixed odd prime q avoiding the table's denominators (1413-1423) is also not mentioned.

All the paper's steps are present. Rows are split cyclically into W role streams of volume V/W, Φ_{A_e} edges run by recursive interchanges, and the result is H<-H+D on every row, scratch rows included. The three-update interchange, s calls, F_k<=(s/W)F_{k-1}+O(1), the geometric sum to O(e^tau) and the fixed-tape parking schedule at O(V) per node match 1491-1589.

The plan follows the paper's reduction (1649-1734): high digits form a row field of range at least W^k, padded to a multiple of W^k; the rest of the width is cut into base-m pieces with geometric cost O(Ve^tau); binary ranges are padded to [q^e], giving O(Vu^tau). Saying the row field comes from the top digits 'of each chunk' is loose (it is h^+ and d^+ joined, range q^{2rho}) but not wrong.

The plan states s_c child calls on f=e/m axes (1904-1906) and H_0^{⊗D}=b^D S_D C^{⊗D} S_D (1929-1930), and it says that binary bases are changed by packed additions. It omits the conjugation by P_M that moves the residual directions to coordinate slots (1849-1862). It also omits the inverse-child identity (C^{-1})^{⊗f}=(-i)^f Z^{⊗f}C^{⊗f}Z^{⊗f} (1885-1888) and the row-addition decomposition of M (1892-1901).

The statement matches: the XORs at positions rho+iK, a third chunk restored, delta_bad=min{1,80(f-1)2^{-K}}, and cost O(V(L^tau+1)) in the family. The route is the paper's: eight shifts flip the parity and restore w; guards fail on B with |B|<=delta_bad M; there are 16 swaps and 8 rotations; the exceptional records are sorted back. The plan never states that S_0 and T_0 agree off B and both preserve B, so that T_0S_0^{-1} permutes only B (2087-2114). That is what makes the sort repair correct.

Node overhead O(V((eK)^tau+1)), children of volume exactly V/W, F(e)<=(s/W)F(e/m)+O((eK)^tau+1), the internal geometric sum and the final lambda' condition all match 2286-2444. Three steps are missing: the bound K<=e^{c/beta}, which makes the overhead O(e^lambda) (2413-2415); the leaf estimate O(e^sigma d^{beta(1-sigma)}) (2421-2430); and the construction of the row index from the first q_0 chunks (2306-2323).

The plan states the layer on D<=d chunks with one truncation, cost O(Vd^{lambda'}) and error below sqrt2 2^{-p}. It follows the proof: the phase-network recursion, the depth recurrence A(e)<=sA(e/m)+E with Delta=C_0 d^{C_1}=o(p) when epsilon C_1<1, the time bound, and the row sum one giving the disk and error bound.

Every element matches the paper. These are contraction, character cancellation by the k+t/2^{v+1} shift (2819-2826), and the DIF recursion writing bit-reversed order. The reverse traversal uses H_0^2=I/2 to give B_tF_t^- and F_t^+B_t^{-1}. The layout L costs O(TpdK) for slot moves, O(Tp pK^{tau-1}) for chunk exchanges and O(Tp ell d^{lambda'}) for layers, with error at most ell truncations.

The plan states and derives the lemma along the paper's route: evaluation at B_0=2^{4p}, the bound |h_j|<B_0/2 giving centered extraction, the negacyclic reduction, and four products in O(rp log(rp)).

The statement matches 3391-3404 in error and cost, and the derivation matches 3414-3495. It has the retained layout (the pointwise product commutes with the record permutation, given in S4's motivation) and the convolution identity with F^+F^-=I/M. It also has the error M(3 delta+eta) and the cost count.

Both lemmas are stated with their key formulas: P_sF_s=2^{2alpha^2}B_0P_tF_tA, error below p^2, time O(tp^{3/2+delta}alpha), and the tensor identity with gamma=2d alpha^2 and the movement cost. The derivation follows the paper: the bound ||N-I||<2^{-alpha^2 theta}, the Neumann series and the normalisations A=S', B_0=D'J'C. The hypothesis theta>p/alpha^4 is not restated in S5.1, but S6.1 has it.

Both identities are stated correctly. The cancellation is derived as in the paper (F^+R=R^{-1}F^+, R commuting with pointwise products, two normalizations). The Bluestein identity is only inferred: the chirp a_j=exp(-pi i sum s_i j_i^2/t_i) and the coefficient computation at 3939-3950 are not given.

Sizes, prime existence in two disjoint intervals, T/2<S<T, the alpha hypotheses and the n^{o(1)} search all follow 4049-4170. The fixed list leaves out tau, lambda, delta and beta. eta=1/(4d) is never defined although S6.1.5 uses it, and the cited prime-count lemma (Rosser-Schoenfeld via HvdH) is not named.

The plan follows the paper's derivation: Phi with mu_i=P_i^{-1}, the isomorphism argument, the triangular coordinates b_i, padding preserved, updates as prefix-controlled shifts in order i=d..1, and the axis reversal by O(d^2) moves costing O(Tpd^2(1+ell^tau)).

The plan states M_C=D_- iota^{-1} M_r(iota D_+ ., iota D_+ .)=(f*g)/T. It derives this from well-definedness, the diagonal invertible map and the wrap check zeta^{k+l}(-1)^h=zeta^j, as at 4303-4342. The computed twist errors are left to S6.7.3.

The source transform (A, chirp transform through the twisted convolution, B_0, scale 2^gamma, exact counterpart RF_s) and the six numbered steps match the paper. So does the explanation that the two factors S undo different normalizations. The opposite procedure by conjugation is implied by S5.4/S6.6.4 but not spelled out.

The plan follows the paper's error chain step by step: E_ring<5TL, 6TL, 8TL, E_s=9*2^gamma TL, 2E_s+2, 3E_s+2, E_w<28*2^gamma T^2L, then 448b 2^{-b+gamma}<1/2. Rounding and the carry recurrence come after. The disk margins are mentioned only in S6.7.5.
The table rows, the margins g_1..g_7, min=2^{-181}=2kappa, o(V) setup and repair, absorption of log factors, and the schoolbook cutoff all match 4808-4995.
S0 says the bound refutes the n log n optimality conjecture in this model. It does not give the content: an eventual lower bound c_A n lg n, refuted by liminf T_A(n)/(n lg n)=0.

errors.says: Over the label field, <t_S,t_T>=|S∩T|-1, so every triple line is nondegenerate and neighbouring triple lines are orthogonal (presented for both networks).
errors.paper: The formula <t_S,t_T>=|S∩T|-1, <t_T,t_T>=2 holds for the bit network's rational form x^T(I-J/9)y. The complex network uses F_2^h with the ordinary dot product, where t_T·t_T=1 and neighbours (even intersection) are orthogonal. The conclusion holds in both, but the formula is not that of the complex label field.

chain: The tree follows the paper's route to the main bound. The plan goes from bank-exchanging network, frames, labels and the rank budget s<Wm, to the explicit exponent tau=1-2^{-50}. From there it runs through the matrix-shear recursion and the phase-frame recursion to the two fast procedures, then through synthetic transforms, resampling, the CRT map and twist, the six-step algorithm, exact recovery and the cost table with margin 2^{-181}=2kappa. It thins in a few places. The scalar network's identity map is only asserted. The complex endpoint corrections and the P_M slot conjugation are left out, and the layer recurrence's leaf and overhead estimates are missing. None of these breaks the chain.

steps.note: The plan gives a fixed linear network on two data banks and scratch wires that sends (X,Y) to (-Y,X) in three stages and restores every scratch wire, with h=100 triples in S1.1.3. It never defines N=binom(h,3)^3 or m=h^3, or says that the banks are indexed by triples; it only refers to an m-dimensional label space and to N. I credited the step for its mechanism, which is borderline.
The plan has frames D_v, edge change D_vD_u^{-1}, the common frame commuting with the pointwise gate, the implemented operator D_out S D_in^{-1}, and intermediate frames free to make edges cheap.

The plan has nondegenerate subspaces of the tensor cube (an m-dimensional label space), comparable labels on every edge, and the central time-3-to-4 edges as the only decreasing ones, each losing h=100.
The plan has rank(P_V-P_U)=dim V-dim U for nested labels, so an edge's cost equals its dimension change, and the N source edges are the exceptions, each costing one extra rank.
The plan has the signed sum Wm-2N, L=Ich, the absolute sum Wm-2N+2L, and s_b=W_b m-N+2L_b.
The plan has L_b/N=100/539 and L_c/N=101/539, both below 1/2, and the deficits N-2L_b>0 and 2N-2L_c>0, so s<Wm.
The plan has the endpoint difference P_{U_a^⊥}-(-P_{U_a})=I_m on every input role (with -P_{U_a} at the sources), so the bit network applies H<-H+D on every role, scratch rows included.
The plan has A=E_1 Pi E_2, a rank-a shear costing exactly a interchanges plus O(V) linear triangular work, and s recursive calls per node in total.
The plan has children of volume V/W, F_k<=(s/W)F_{k-1}+O(1), s/W<m^tau with tau=1-2^{-50} from eta>20*2^{-50} and log m<20, and F_k=O(e^tau).

central.summary: P12 reconstructs all nine steps of the central saving in order. The fixed bank-exchanging network becomes frames and nested labels, ranks equal dimension changes with N source exceptions, and the budget s_b=W_b m-N+2L_b is strictly below W_b m because L/N=100/539<1/2. The endpoint identity gives the shear on every role, each rank unit becomes one recursive interchange, and the recurrence with s/W<m^{1-2^{-50}} gives O(e^tau). The only weak point is C1: N and m=h^3 are used but never defined.
